deviation_summary: During Phase D, after rebuilding the successor artifact index (old sha256:fbeedef1... -> new sha256:06496a6a...) to fold in the Phase C regenerated storyboard frames, three fail-closed guards blocked re-running the qualification chain for the SAME revision id with a CHANGED index. The Phase D agent hand-cleared five pieces of derived/mutable state (one ArangoDB active-pointer document, one immutable queue terminal event, and three immutable qualification receipts) to let prepare/verify/activation re-run to PASS. This audit reconstructs exactly what was cleared and whether any evidentiary content was lost.

index_change.reason: Phase C regenerated 8 storyboard frames were folded into the index and phase bindings; the montage frames were demoted to superseded_frame optional evidence. Same revision id, changed index.

The gitignored state/ receipts (e.g. pipeline_step_memory_receipt_rev_successor_943b01ecd9a3.json, identity_source_successor_receipt_rev_successor_943b01ecd9a3.json) were NOT among the deleted items and remain present on disk.

verdict.reasoning: All five cleared items were derived/mutable qualification state bound to the superseded OLD artifact index, not primary or irreproducible evidence. The four file-based items (terminal event + three receipts) are preserved byte-for-byte in git history at commit a97c734e and their old content hashes were reverified during this audit. The single ArangoDB item was a single-slot current-active pointer that is deterministically re-derivable from the committed old activation receipt; by design it is overwritten on every activation. The frozen source revision rev_upstream_bf3b05d47fb8 and all Phase C regenerated-frame evidence were untouched. No evidentiary content is unrecoverable.
verdict.residual_risk: The deletion was performed ad hoc via direct ArangoDB access and manual file removal, leaving no supersession receipt binding old->new at the time. Recoverability here is incidental (the state happened to be committed at a97c734e and the pointer happened to be re-derivable), not a property the ad hoc procedure guaranteed. This audit codifies a sanctioned supersession path so future rebuilt-index re-qualification never depends on that luck.

proves: the exact five items cleared during Phase D are enumerated with their pre-deletion identity and content hashes

every cleared item's pre-deletion content is recoverable: the four files from git commit a97c734e (hashes reverified) and the one ArangoDB pointer by deterministic re-derivation from the committed old activation receipt
the deleted qualification receipts were the git-tracked revision-tree receipts, not the gitignored state/ receipts
the current PASS receipts and the live ArangoDB active pointer are the coherent replacement bound to the rebuilt index sha256:06496a6a...
the frozen revision rev_upstream_bf3b05d47fb8 was not touched
does_not_prove: that the ad hoc deletion was a sanctioned procedure at the time it was performed (it was not; it is retroactively audited here)
that the rebuilt index or the regenerated storyboard frames are themselves correct (that is the acceptance-rung evidence, out of scope for this deletion audit)
